deliverables.title: Acute Jaundice: 9 Time-Critical Exclusions
deliverables.visual_concept: Central jaundice patient illustration; 9 labeled exclusion branches radiating outward. Each branch shows the recognition pattern and the killer action.

items.pattern: Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice (Charcot) ± hypotension / AMS (Reynolds)
items.killer_action: Ascending cholangitis — antibiotics within 1 hour, GI for emergent ERCP

items.pattern: Any acetaminophen exposure (acute or chronic supra-therapeutic) in last 72 h
items.killer_action: APAP hepatotoxicity — Rumack-Matthew + NAC threshold; treat early, treat empirically
Acute liver failure — Kings College criteria, NAC, transplant center NOW
Massive hemolysis (TTP/HUS/MAHA/sickle/G6PD/AIHA) — type and cross, heme STAT

items.pattern: AST/ALT >1000 + recent shock / cardiac arrest / hypotension
items.killer_action: Ischemic hepatitis ("shock liver") — fix the upstream perfusion failure

items.pattern: Painless jaundice + weight loss + age ≥50 (± Courvoisier sign)
items.killer_action: Malignant biliary obstruction until proven otherwise — imaging + GI/onc

items.pattern: Age <40 + hemolysis + low alk phos + AST:ALT >2 ± Kayser-Fleischer rings
items.killer_action: Wilson disease de novo presentation — ceruloplasmin, 24h urine copper, hepatology

items.pattern: Abdominal pain + ascites + hepatomegaly + hypercoagulable state
items.killer_action: Budd-Chiari syndrome — Doppler US, CT venogram, anticoag, hepatology

items.pattern: Young female + AST/ALT very high + ↑IgG + ANA/SMA positive
items.killer_action: Autoimmune hepatitis flare — steroids per hepatology, biopsy planning

deliverables.title: Acute Jaundice: 5-Module Pathway
deliverables.visual_concept: 5 numbered boxes left to right with arrows. Color-coded by urgency tier. 2-3 bullet labels per box.

items.summary: Gestalt sick check + West Haven grade + 4-question screen (APAP, Charcot, encephalopathy, recent shock). Resus parallel if unstable, encephalopathic, or coagulopathic.
Pick the most acute hit. Each branch links to its deep-dive or focused result + tells you the next 5-min action.
IV + NPO + ondansetron + APAP-free analgesia + broad hepatic panel + APAP level (always) + viral / autoimmune / hemolysis workup. Reassess at 60-90 min.
RUQ US first for nearly everyone. MRCP for biliary tree mapping. CT/CTA for mass / vascular workup. ERCP is therapeutic. "Normal imaging" does not rule out hepatocellular causes.

deliverables.title: Acute Jaundice: 10 Do-NOTs
deliverables.visual_concept: 2x5 grid of red-bordered warning cards. Each card has a number, a short imperative verb, and a one-line teaser.

items.imperative: Do NOT skip the APAP level on any altered + jaundiced patient
items.teaser: APAP is the most common cause of acute liver failure in the US.

items.imperative: Do NOT correct INR with FFP in ALF unless actively bleeding
items.teaser: INR is the prognostic marker that drives King\

items.imperative: Do NOT delay antibiotics for the ERCP slot in cholangitis
items.teaser: Charcot triad → blood cultures × 2 → antibiotics within 1 hour.

items.imperative: Do NOT mistake Reynolds pentad for ALF encephalopathy
items.teaser: Septic shock from cholangitis presents with AMS + jaundice + hypotension + fever.

items.imperative: Do NOT discharge "painless jaundice in age ≥50" as viral hepatitis
items.teaser: Painless jaundice + weight loss + age ≥50 + cholestatic LFT pattern (alk phos / GGT out of proportion) = malignant biliary obstruction until proven otherwise.

items.imperative: Do NOT miss Wilson disease in the young ALF patient
items.teaser: Young patient + ALF + LOW alk phos + alk-phos-to-bili ratio <4 + Coombs-negative hemolysis = Wilson disease.

items.imperative: Do NOT forget glucose monitoring q1h in ALF
items.teaser: Hepatocyte gluconeogenesis failure causes hypoglycemia that is silent in the encephalopathic patient.

items.imperative: Do NOT give platelets in suspected TTP
items.teaser: TTP pentad (MAHA + thrombocytopenia + fever + AMS + renal failure) — platelets fuel microthrombi and worsen end-organ ischemia.

items.imperative: Do NOT use the hub as a treatment playbook
items.teaser: The hub is a triage map.

items.imperative: Do NOT discharge without written return precautions and a booked 48-72 h recheck
items.teaser: Even benign-pattern jaundice (Gilbert, stable cirrhosis at baseline, very mild non-progressive viral hepatitis) requires hepatology or PCP follow-up within 48-72 hours.
